title: Inverse Gysin pinnings make the constant sheaf potential on a regular scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $T$ be a Noetherian excellent regular scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme]; $T$ need not be connected. For $x\in T$ put $c_T(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{T,x}$, the Krull dimension of the local ring [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,x}$ be the closed-point inclusion. Use the dimension functions, twists, supported costalks $R\Gamma_x$, normalized residue transitions and pinned potential complexes of [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Then $-c_T$ is a dimension function on $T$. Let $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}:\Lambda(-c_T(x))[-2c_T(x)]\xrightarrow{\sim}i_x^!\Lambda=R\Gamma_x\Lambda_T$ be the absolute-purity Gysin isomorphism of the closed immersion $i_x$ of [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus], and put $p_x=\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}$. These pinnings make $\Lambda_T$ a pinned potential dualizing complex for $-c_T$. For every integer $m$, the pinnings $p_x(m)[2m]$ make $\Lambda_T(m)[2m]$ a pinned potential dualizing complex for $x\mapsto m-c_T(x)$. At a generic point of $T$ the pinning of $\Lambda_T$ is the identity.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.1.1 (inverse Gysin pinnings, printed p.265) and Proposition 2.4.4.1 (potentiality on a regular excellent scheme with dimension function -codim, printed pp.267-268); twist and shift as in the proof of Lemma 4.3.1.1

proof.text: We will use the prime-power Gysin and finite-detection statements with exponent $n=1$. At that exponent the definitions [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex, def-per-potential-dualizing] agree under $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z=\mathbf F_\ell$: both use the supported-kernel right derived functor, the same roots-of-unity twists, geometric-fibre pinnings, and the equation $p_{\bar y}=p_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}$. Their normalized transition is the same map: on the normalized strict-local curve both average over wild inertia, evaluate at $\sigma$ and inversely at $1-\sigma$, then multiply by the inverse of the closed residue-field degree. Thus no comparison with an adic category or an unnormalized residue is being assumed.

source.place: XVII Definitions 1.2.3.1, 1.3.1, 1.4.1 and 2.1.1–2.1.2, specialized to n=ell

proof.text: By [rem-pc-regular-normal], $T$ is a finite disjoint union of open and closed integral regular components. Every specialization lies in one component, so fix an immediate geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ in one of them. Excellence includes universal catenarity [def-exc-excellent-ring], and [lem-per-geometric-immediate-catenary] gives a saturated inclusion $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ in an affine domain around $x$. In its localization at $\mathfrak q$, concatenate a saturated prime chain from $(0)$ to $\mathfrak p$ with this final inclusion. The bounded-chain and equal-saturated-length conditions of catenarity say that the resulting length is the dimension at $\mathfrak q$, whereas the original length is the dimension at $\mathfrak p$. Hence $c_T(x)=c_T(y)+1$, so $-c_T(y)=-c_T(x)+1$. This is precisely the dimension-function condition of [def-per-potential-dualizing]. It applies separately on every component without a connectedness assumption.

source.place: XIV Proposition 2.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.4; XVII Definition 2.1.1

proof.text: For $x\in T$, the ring $\mathcal O_{T,x}$ is regular local. Its prime localizations are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], and it is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. The residue field is regular of dimension zero. The closed point immersion $i_x$ is finite between Noetherian regular affine schemes, so [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] at $n=1$ gives its Gysin isomorphism of virtual dimension $-c_T(x)$. This is the absolute-purity class named in [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus], whose regular-immersion class has that normalization. Set $p_x=\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}$. Localization and etale compatibility of these classes make the pinnings intrinsic and identify their geometric restrictions. They are putative pinnings as defined in [def-per-potential-dualizing]; their residue compatibility is proved below. At a generic point $\eta$ the local ring is a field, $c_T(\eta)=0$ and $i_\eta$ is the identity, so identity normalization in [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] gives $p_\eta=1$.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.1.1; XVI Theorem 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.2

proof.text:
Fix an immediate geometric specialization and put $X=T_{( ar x)}$, $d=c_T(x)$. Its local ring is regular of dimension $d$ by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular, lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension]; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] makes $X$ regular as a scheme. The localization comparisons of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection] transport our putative pinnings and their residue square to this Noetherian excellent $X$. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced closure of the image of $ ar y$, and $
u:V	o C$ its normalization. By [lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction], $C$ is excellent integral strictly henselian of dimension one, $
u$ is finite surjective, and $V$ is a strictly henselian DVR trait; its generic point is unchanged and its closed residue extension is purely inseparable of invertible degree. The finite normalization algebra is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. A DVR is regular local (dimension one and principal maximal ideal), so $V$ is regular by the localization lemma. Put $L=i^!\Lambda_X$ with its induced putative pinnings. By [lem-per-putative-finite-detection], the square we must check is exactly the square for $L$ on $C$, and it can be tested on $
u^!L$ before any potentiality is known.

source.place: XVII proof of Proposition 2.4.4.1, printed p.268: reduction to the curve and its normalization

proof.text:
Write $h=i
u:V	o X$. It is finite between regular affine schemes. The quasi-finite formula in [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] computes its locally constant virtual dimension at the closed point as $a=1-d$, hence on the whole trait as $a$. Its purity map is $\operatorname{Cl}_h:\Lambda_V(a)[2a]\xrightarrow{\sim}h^!\Lambda_X=
u^!L$. Check the specified pinnings at each of the two points $v$ of $V$. Put $z=h(v)$ and $\pi_v:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)	o\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$. After localization, the equality $h i_v=i_z\pi_v$ and Gysin composition give
$$i_v^!\operatorname{Cl}_h\circ\operatorname{Cl}_{i_v}(a)[2a]=\pi_v^!\operatorname{Cl}_{i_z}\circ\operatorname{Cl}_{\pi_v},$$
with the additive twist-shifts understood. The induced pinning in [lem-per-putative-finite-detection] is $\operatorname{Cl}_{\pi_v}^{-1}\circ\pi_v^!p_z$. Compose this with the displayed equality and $p_z=\operatorname{Cl}_{i_z}^{-1}$: the right side cancels to the identity. Thus $\operatorname{Cl}_h$ identifies the induced pinnings on $
u^!L$ with $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_v}^{-1}(a)[2a]$ on $\Lambda_V(a)[2a]$. Their dimension values are $a-1=-d$ at the closed point and $a$ at the generic point. This proves the required pinning comparison directly from composition, without assuming that the ambient constant sheaf is potential.

source.place: XVII Lemma 2.4.3.4 and its Gysin composition square, printed pp.266–267

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-trait-gysin-residue] at $n=1$ on $V$. It gives $\operatorname{sp}_{\eta,v}(\Lambda_V)=\operatorname{Cl}_{i_v}(1)[2]$, including the sign. Since the generic pinning is the identity, the closed pinning satisfies
$$p_v(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\eta,v}=\operatorname{Cl}_{i_v}^{-1}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{Cl}_{i_v}(1)[2]=1=p_\eta.$$
The twists are etale locally free lines by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. On this strict trait a trivializing etale neighbourhood over the closed point has a section by [lem-sbc-strict-henselian-etale-neighbourhood-section], so its basis pulls back to $V$. In this basis tensoring by $(a)$ and shifting by $2a$ leaves the linear maps of the residue model of [def-per-potential-dualizing] unchanged; averaging, evaluation and the normalizing scalar all commute with the basis change. The shifted square therefore commutes as well. Consequently the shifted regular pinnings on $\Lambda_V(a)[2a]$ are potential, and Step 5 identifies them with those of $\nu^!L$.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.2.1(a), using the residue model of sections 1.2.2–1.2.3

proof.text: The finite-surjective reflection assertion of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection], at exponent $n=1$, applied to $\nu:V\to C$ and the putative complex $L$, proves that $L$ is potential. The same node identifies this residue square with the original square for $\Lambda_T$ at $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$. Thus $p_{\bar y}=p_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}$. As the chosen immediate specialization was arbitrary, [def-per-potential-dualizing] now says exactly that the inverse-Gysin pinnings of Step 3 make $\Lambda_T$ potential for $-c_T$. This argument uses reflection from a putative complex, not a pullback assertion requiring potentiality in advance. If $T$ is empty both the dimension condition and all pinning conditions are vacuous; otherwise every specialization was handled in its open and closed component in Step 2.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.3.3 and the proof of Proposition 2.4.4.1

proof.text: For $m\in\mathbf Z$, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] makes $\Lambda_T(m)$ a locally free line, also for negative $m$, and identifies all of its point pullbacks. The costalk identification $R\Gamma_x(\Lambda_T(m)[2m])\cong(R\Gamma_x\Lambda_T)(m)[2m]$ follows locally from the supported-kernel definition in [def-per-potential-dualizing]: after trivializing the line, tensor is an exact rank-one autoequivalence, preserves injectives and the supported kernel, and hence gives that identification on injective resolutions. The identifications glue because changes of basis are units commuting with every linear map. Define the new pinning by $p_x(m)[2m]$, with target $\Lambda(m-c_T(x))[2(m-c_T(x))]$. To check a residue square, choose a basis on $T_{(\bar x)}$ using [lem-sbc-strict-henselian-etale-neighbourhood-section], and pull it to the reduced curve, its normalization and its geometric fibres. In the defining transition of [def-per-potential-dualizing], averaging, both evaluations and the inverse residue degree commute with this basis. The square is precisely the already commuting square of Step 7 tensored and shifted. The shift $2m$ is even, so no shift sign changes this equality. Finally adding $m$ to a dimension function preserves its defining equality. These are the required twisted pinned potential complexes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q12-8ede2309a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read ILO XVII 2.4.1.1, 2.4.2.1, 2.4.3.1-2.4.3.4 and 2.4.4.1 (printed pp. 265-268). The item statement matches them hypothesis by hypothesis: Noetherian regular excellent T, l invertible, delta = -codim, pinning = inverse of Cl_{i_x}. The extra clauses are true: the twist-shift (as in 4.3.1.1), the identity pinning at generic points, and the disconnected case. The proof follows ILO's route: strict localization, then C and its normalization, the Gysin composition of 2.4.3.4, the trait case 2.4.2.1(a) through lem-per-trait-gysin-residue, and finite-surjective reflection through lem-per-putative-finite-detection. Step 1 states the identification of the Z/l^n definition at n=1 with the F_l definition; I compared both definitions and both pairs of costalk and trait-model lemmas, and they are textually identical at n=1, so the step is elementary and the Z/l^n citations at n=1 are legitimate. Step 2: catenarity gives ht q = ht p + 1, applied componentwise via rem-pc-regular-normal. Step 3: the Gysin class of lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus is the absolute-purity class, since that node's proof uses lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity. Step 5: the virtual dimension 1-d is consistent at both points of V, and the pinning targets -d and -c_T(y) match. Steps 6 and 8: twisting by a trivialized line with an even shift introduces no sign. Edge cases checked: empty T, a field, an excellent DVR, disconnected T, m<0. No cycle, no new nodes, no SGA citation. All seven declared tool_uses are generic commutative algebra or etale-twist facts; I accept them. Batch-5 flags, none a RETURN: def-per-potential-dualizing-complex and lem-per-trait-gysin-residue reach the trace-formula chapter only through lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance, which is Stacks 05WR/0GIP (invariance of strict localization under ind-etale maps), a generic fact. lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction reaches lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence, which is pure algebra (Stacks 092X/09XK). Neither is a step of the trace formula or of Poincare duality.
